content.comment_body: Hello, I'm trying to use a micro SD card (SanDisk Ultra 64 GB, FAT32) to copy the configuration from my [product_name]. After powering off, inserting the card, and powering on again, I can't find the 'Card' menu. Could the issue be that 64 GB is too large for this device or is there another problem? Appreciate any advice! [user_name]
Yes, 64 GB is too large. You should create a partition up to 32 GB and format it with FAT32.
I assumed that entering the diagnostics menu and seeing the card status as 'OK' would mean it works...

I've only used SD cards up to 32 GB, formatted as FAT32, and haven't experienced any issues. I noticed in your screenshots the menu language is set to German. Do you currently reside in Germany or speak German?
I tried a 2 GB micro SD card today, formatted with FAT32 and a 4096-byte allocation unit, but still don't see the 'Card' menu. I'm in Germany now but don't speak German.
I found an old 2 GB micro SD card and formatted it with these settings, and had no problems using it.

If the card menu doesn't appear after inserting the SD card, check for any bent pins in the card holder and ensure the card is fully inserted. The card holder design could be improved, so many are hoping for a better version in the future. Regards, [user_name]
In a previous comment from 10/29/2019 2:33 PM, [user_name] mentioned that the diagnostics menu displayed "SD Card ok".

The issue is resolved. Access to the 'Card' menu requires switching the system to 'stop' or 'off' mode using the upper menu. My system was always running. Changing the operating state solved the problem. Additionally, administrative mode is needed rather than user mode.

I'm always in admin mode, so I forget that user mode only shows part of the menu. Thanks for your update. It's best to insert and remove the card in stop state to prevent data loss or unexpected actions during ongoing processes. Regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: Users struggled to access the 'Card' menu on their [product_name] when attempting to use micro SD cards of various formats and capacities. The critical factors for SD card operations were the system's status (must be stopped) and the access rights (administrative mode required). Lack of clear UI feedback and guidance led to confusion among users.
analysis.user_expectations: Users anticipated immediate menu access when inserting any FAT32 SD card, regardless of system state or card size, and wanted clear and direct feedback from the device.
